answer_raw:
**Florianópolis** offers the most significant stretch for a $4,000 monthly budget, though Medellín provides a competitive middle ground and Lisbon represents the highest cost of living among the three.

The money stretches furthest in **Florianópolis**, where a single person can live for roughly **$1,500 per month** including rent, food, and transport as of June 2026 [3]. In contrast, a single person in **Medellín** faces monthly costs of roughly **R$9,321** (approx. **$2,300** at current exchange rates) as of November c. 2026 [4]. **Lisbon** is the most expensive, with monthly costs for one person reaching roughly **R$12,200** (approx. **$3,000**) as of November 2026 [4], or needing **€4,800** to maintain a certain standard compared to much lower costs elsewhere [6, undated].

Rent profiles for each city:

| City | Rent Profile | Source/Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Florianópolis** | Typically **€500–€800** per month [1, 2026] or **R$2,500–R$3,800** for a 1-br in a good area [5, 2026]. | [1], [5] |
| **Medellín** | A central apartment runs roughly **R$7,387** as of November 2026 [4]. | [4] |
| **Lisbon** | Averages **€1,401.56** per month [1, 2026] or roughly **R$9,037** for a central apartment [4, 2026]. | [1], [4] |

In **Florianópolis**, the Brazilian Digital Nomad Visa (VITEM XIV) allows remote workers to secure a 1-year renewable permit with simple income proof of approximately **$1,500/mo** as of 2026 [1]. While **Lisbon** offers higher safety (85/100) and livability (67/100) compared to **Medellín** (66/100) or **Florianópolis** (82/100 safety), it is the most expensive option [1][2].
